chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Ala' ibn al-Fudayl, who said:

I asked him about a man performing Tamattu' who circled the Kaaba, then entered the state of Ihram for Hajj before shortening his hair. He said: His Tamattu' is invalidated; it is a Hajj that is 'mutabathala' (flawed/compensated). The meaning in this report is that we interpret it as applying to one who did that intentionally. As for one who did it unintentionally, his Tamattu' is not invalidated, according to what the earlier reports contained.

key_terms.أَهَلَّ بِالْحَجِّ: He entered the state of Ihram for Hajj
key_terms.مُبْتَلَوَةً: Flawed or compensated (a specific type of Hajj)
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعٍ: A pilgrim performing Tamattu' (Umrah then Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a Mutamatti' enters Ihram for Hajj before shortening his hair?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from al-Saffar, highlighting the juristic distinction between intentional and unintentional errors in the sequence of Hajj rites. The Imam clarifies that while deliberate premature Ihram invalidates the Umrah portion (rendering it 'mutabathala'), the principle of *al-asl fi al-ahkam al-sahha* (presumption of validity) protects the pilgrim if the act was done in forgetfulness, aligning with earlier narrations.
